title: The history of extreme sports

paragraphs.text: Section four. You'll hear a part of lecture about history of extreme sport. First, you have some time to look at questions thirty-one to forty.

Extreme sports are non-traditional sports and activities that require participants to combine athletic skill with pronounced risk. It is difficult to determine exactly when the term extreme sports came to refer to certain modern sports. While many extreme sports, such as deep diving and surfing, have usually been part of human history, so many extreme sports are often called lifestyle sports. They often involve speed, height, physical commitment. The practice of extreme sports can involve some risks, injuries, and even death if the athlete made a serious mistake. Technological advances have brought more reliable equipment, which making various sports a safer activity. The worldwide spread of extreme sports is attributed to the media. Televisions and movies have been responsible for gaining a widespread participation in extreme sports.

In the nineteenth century, the acceptance by workforce extended. For those men with lower leisure preference, Sundays were generally free from labor. One extreme sport was studied by workers from a company in its free time. Employers commonly believe this leisure activity increased productivity, and most importantly, increased workers' loyalty to the company.

The nineteenth century is considered by many to be the period when the truly modern game emerged. The changes that primarily spurred this modernization were to be the equipment of the game. Other sports, such as golf, was popularized and regularly attended by the upper classes and nobility. Early golf clubs were made of materials similar to today's club, wood and iron. However, the biggest difference between the old golf clubs and modern ones was the use.

In the twentieth century, you may be wondering, what is it that attracts people to extreme sports in comparison to many traditional sports like football or basketball? One of the few things that coaches, players, and fans of nearly every competitive team sports seem to agree on these days is that there are too many regulations for these games. Secondly, most of the people involved in extreme sports do not feel the need for constant training and physical conditioning of their body. This leads to the stage where people who love extreme sports do not take part in those games as they grow older.

Finally, participants described how extreme sports experiencing, controlling, and overcome fear made them positively change everyday life. A mountain climber described dealing with fear as empowering and feeling very at peace afterwards.
A base jumper described the pursuit as ultimate metaphor for jumping into the life rather than standing on the edge quivering.

In assessing the use of taxpayers' funds in bidding for major event or building a new stadium, or even trying to secure a new license for sports team, young sports participants clearly want government to put their emphasis on entertainment sports. Everyone can participate, everyone will have fun, and everyone can be involved. Individual competition, limitations, requirements, and other concerns simply aren't part of the equation. Young people dealt with self-existence to find authorities which are responsible for sport.

Combating racism in sport falls to everyone, including public authorities. Young people's responses to the changing world and their unique way is building their own community. Extreme sports are huge craze today. The psychology behind its popularity seems to be human nature to take risk for thrill,
and the adventure continues to attract masses.
